before.en:
Al-Biruni worked on astronomy, mathematics, chronology and the comparison of religious and intellectual traditions. His life crossed changes of political patronage in Khwarazm and the Ghaznavid world. Observations and dated statements in his own works provide anchors that are more secure than some reconstructions of his movements.

His account of Indian knowledge involved language learning, comparison and efforts to understand systems different from his own. Such work should not be reduced either to an isolated genius or to a claim that every description was impartial. Scholars can identify both methods and the limits of available evidence. Linking this biography with Aryabhata and Ibn Sina situates intellectual exchange across regions, while the representative pin does not imply a permanent residence or a continuous, independently surveyed route.
before.zh:
比鲁尼研究天文、数学、编年，并比较宗教和思想传统。生涯跨越花剌子模与伽色尼世界中政治资助者的变化。其本人著作中的观测和纪年，为生平提供比某些迁移重建更稳固的锚点。

对印度知识的叙述涉及语言学习、比较以及理解不同体系的努力。这些工作不能缩为孤立天才的故事，也不表示每项描述都不带立场。研究者可以同时辨析方法与现有证据局限。与阿耶波多、伊本·西那相连，可以把思想交换置于跨区域环境；代表性点位不表示永久居所或连续、独立测绘的路线。

after.en:
Al-Biruni worked on astronomy, mathematics, chronology and the comparison of religious and intellectual traditions. His life crossed changes of political patronage in Khwarazm and the Ghaznavid world. His account of Indian knowledge drew on language learning and comparison across intellectual traditions.

A later manuscript at Princeton preserves Ibn Sina’s letter addressed to al-Biruni. Its catalogue identifies two sequences of ten and seven philosophical questions and answers. Copied in a manuscript dated 1279, the opening page makes their scholarly exchange visible as a text transmitted between generations.
after.zh:
比鲁尼研究天文、数学、编年，并比较宗教与思想传统。其生涯跨越花剌子模与伽色尼世界中政治资助者的变化；对印度知识的叙述则依靠语言学习与不同思想传统之间的比较。

普林斯顿保存的一部后世手稿收录伊本·西那致比鲁尼的书信。目录指出其中有两组哲学问答，分别包含十问与七问。目录定年为1279年的手稿开篇，让这场学术交流以历代传抄的文本形式呈现在眼前。

manuscriptMetadata.label: Abstract
value: Collection of philosophical texts, mainly from Avicenna and al-Fārābī.

manuscriptMetadata.label: Alternative
value: Rasāʼil Ibn [Sīnā] wa-al-Fār[ābī ... wa-] al-Rāzī ... wa-Aflā ...

manuscriptMetadata.label: Contents
value: 3. fol 3b-12b: Risālah ilá Abī Rayḥān Muḥammad al-Bīrūnī / Avicenna. Two series of respectively 10 and 7 questions and answers on several philosophical matters.
4. fol. 13b-17a: Maqālah fī khaṭaʼ man qāla inna shayʼan huwa jawhar wa-ʻaraḍ maʻan / Avicenna.
6. fol. 68b-70Ab: Ajwibah ʻan ʻashr masāʼil / Avicenna.
7. fol. 70Ab-71a: Risālah li-Aflāṭūn fī al-radd ʻalá man qāla inna al-insān talāshā wa-faniya.
8. fol. 71b-89b: Kitāb fī marātib al-ʻulūm / Abū Naṣr Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Fārābī.
9. fol. 90b-93a: Maqālah fī qawānīn ṣināʻat al-shuʻarāʼ / Fārābī.
10. fol. 93b-125a: al-Kitāb fī mabādiʼ ārāʼ ahl al-madīnah al-fāḍilah / Fārābī.
11. fol. 125b-130a: Tafsīr li-baʻḍ suwar kalām Allāh / Avicenna.
12. fol. 130b-142a: Kitāb Taḥqīr al-ladhdhāt / Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī. Treatise in three parts (qism) on the vileness of the pleasures of this world.
16. fol. 159a-160a: Risālah fī īḍāḥ barāhīn mustanbaṭah fī masāʼil ʻawīṣah / Avicenna.
17. fol. 160b-175b: Kitāb Mukhtaṣar Anūlūṭīqā al-ūlá / Fārābī. Incomplete: fol. 161 and 166 are blank later paper.
18. fol. 176a-177a: Risālah fī ḥarakat al-kull / Alexander of Aphrodisias.
20. fol. 266b-270a: Kitāb fī ibṭāl aḥkām al-nujūm / Fārābī. Treatise refuting astrology.
21. fol. 270b-293b: Kitāb fī al-ārāʼ al-ṭabīʻīyah allatī taqūl bihā al-ḥukamāʼ / Pseudo-Plutarchus. Arabic translation of the pseudo-Plutarchian Placita philosophorum.
22. fol. 294a-295a: al-Maqālah fī al-jihah allatī yaṣiḥḥu ʻalayhā al-qawl fī aḥkām al-nujūm / Fārābī. Treatise on the question of the validity of astrology.

23. fol. 295b-305a: Risālah ilá al-Iskandar fī al-ʻālam wa-al-makhlūqāt [De mundo] / Pseudo-Aristotle. Ps.-Aristoteles De Mundo, translated from Syriac by ʻĪsā ibn Ibrāhīm al-Nafīsī al-Mutaṭabbib.
24. fol. 305b-310b: Sharḥ Waṣāyā Fūthāghūras al-faylasūf. Commentary on the Golden verses of Pythagoras, incomplete at end.
